To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Automated irrigation based on threshold canopy temperature is a promising method for reducing water use in cotton.

(1) automated irrigation based on canopy temperature can be used to produce maximum lint yield, (2) the threshold temperature that produces maximum yield is 28° C when water supply is not limiting, (3) the threshold temperature can be raised to 30° C without significantly affecting yield, and (4) water use efficiency and cotton maturity are improved by raising threshold temperature.
automated drip irrigation of cotton can be controlled by continuously measuring canopy temperature and computing average canopy temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of canopy temperature as a means of controlling an irrigation system in a cotton field.
the development and evaluation of an automated irrigation system that is based on the measurement of cotton canopy temperature.
the development of an automated irrigation system based on the threshold canopy temperature concept.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a threshold of 28° C is optimum for cotton irrigation management.
the 28° and 30° threshold temperatures were most appropriate for the cotton production conditions of the Texas High Plains.
a 28° threshold is optimum for maximum yield and a 30° threshold would be optimum under limited water conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
automated irrigation based on canopy temperature can reduce water use and increase water use efficiency while maintaining lint yield.
automated irrigation based on canopy temperature is a feasible alternative to traditional scheduling techniques.
the 28° and 30° threshold temperatures were most appropriate for cotton production in our environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the threshold canopy temperature should be selected based on the season length and water availability.
the 28°C canopy temperature threshold is the best for maximum lint yield.
the 28°C threshold temperature should provide maximum lint yields in areas where water supply and growing season length do not constrain production.
